title: The agent that forgot Postgres
scenario: A team runs a long coding agent on Claude. They wrote their own summarizer: when the context reaches 600,000 tokens, it replaces the whole history with a summary. After one compaction, the agent undoes an earlier decision. You review the run log (exhibit).
exhibit:
AGENT RUN (Claude, own summarizer, trigger at 600k tokens)

TURN 140  decision: use Postgres, not SQLite
          (the report job needs row locking)
TURN 212  context at 600k -> compaction runs

SUMMARY PROMPT
  Summarize the conversation in 5 short bullet points.

SUMMARY
  - Migrated the user table
  - Added login tests
  - Fixed 3 failing tests
  - Updated the README
  - Next: build the report job

TURN 231  agent: I'll store report rows in SQLite
          to keep things simple.

CONTEXT JUST BEFORE COMPACTION
  tool results (file reads, test logs)   71%
  messages and reasoning                  29%

questions.prompt: Why did the agent switch back to SQLite?

options.text: SQLite is the better fit for a report job, so the agent corrected itself.
options.explanation: The log says the report job needs row locking, which is why the team chose Postgres. The agent did not weigh that; it no longer knew it.

options.text: Context rot: 600,000 tokens was too many for the model to read.
options.explanation: After compaction the context was small. The decision was missing from it, not hidden in it.

options.text: The summary dropped the Postgres decision, so the agent lost it.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic warns that overly aggressive compaction can lose subtle but critical context whose importance only shows up later.

options.text: Compaction always deletes decisions, so long agents cannot keep them.
options.explanation: Anthropic's own example keeps architectural decisions in the summary. What gets kept depends on the summary prompt.

questions.prompt: How should the team improve their summary prompt, following Anthropic's advice?

options.text: Tune it on complex traces: maximize recall first, then trim for precision.
options.explanation: Right. Capture every relevant piece first (decisions, open bugs, implementation details), then remove extra content.

options.text: Make it stricter: ask for 3 bullet points so the summary stays small.
options.explanation: A tighter limit drops even more. Anthropic's advice is to maximize recall first, not to shrink the summary further.

options.text: Ask only for the next step, since the past is already done.
options.explanation: Past decisions shape the next steps. Anthropic's summary keeps architectural decisions and unresolved bugs for that reason.

options.text: Ask for the summary as JSON so the agent can parse it more easily.
options.explanation: The format is not the gap. The 5-bullet limit left no room for the Postgres decision in any format.

questions.prompt: 71% of the context was old tool results. Which lighter step could delay compaction?

options.text: Raise the trigger to 900,000 tokens so compaction runs less often.
options.explanation: That keeps more stale results around. The Claude docs note that response quality degrades as a conversation grows.

options.text: Delete the user's earlier messages and keep all the tool results.
options.explanation: The messages hold decisions like the Postgres choice. The old tool results are the part Anthropic calls safe to clear.

options.text: Move the tool results into the system prompt, where they cost less.
options.explanation: Moving them does not make them smaller, so the context is just as full as before.

options.text: Clear the oldest tool results with Claude's context editing.
options.explanation: Right. The `clear_tool_uses_20250919` strategy replaces old results with placeholder text. Anthropic calls tool result clearing one of the safest, lightest forms of compaction.

questions.prompt: Another team runs the same agent on OpenAI and calls `/responses/compact`. What should their code do with the response?

options.text: Read the compaction item and show it to users as a progress report.
options.explanation: OpenAI says the compaction item is opaque and not intended to be human-interpretable.

options.text: Pass the returned window into the next request unchanged.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says not to prune the compact endpoint's output: the returned window is the canonical next context window.

options.text: Keep only the compaction item and drop the other returned items.
options.explanation: The returned window can include retained items from the previous window. OpenAI says to pass it as-is.

options.text: Summarize the compaction item again with their own prompt.
options.explanation: The item is opaque, so there is nothing readable to summarize. The window goes into the next call as returned.
